newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Asterix quits retirement to rave reviews.
newsitem.headline: France's Asterix quits retirement to rave reviews.

text.p: Fans of Asterix the Gaul queued in bookshops on Thursday after the comic strip hero came out of retirement to rave reviews, fighting Romans on a voyage to the lost continent of Atlantis.

"The magic potion still works," La Chaine Info television said of "Asterix and Obelix all at Sea," the 30th book in a series that has sold 280 million copies worldwide. "A real treat," echoed the daily Le Parisien.

The book, featuring Asterix's dim-witted sidekick Obelix magically reduced to child size, went on sale amid a blitz of publicity with an initial print run of eight million copies in 15 languages, one of the biggest in publishing history.

The book is the first since 1991 about a tiny village resisting the Roman invasion of Gaul in 50 BC with the help of a strength-giving magic potion brewed by the druid Getafix. The series has sold 100 million more copies than the Tintin books.
"It's going well. We expect to sell a huge number," said Philippe Salmon, manager of a Gilbert Jeune bookstore in central Paris beside a large display of the new book.
In another Paris bookshop, one man queuing to buy the book asked a sales assistant: "Do you think you've got enough?" She answered "I don't know, it's been crazy today."

Author and illustrator Albert Uderzo, 69, went back to the drawing board saying he regretted announcing in 1994 that he had retired after losing a lawsuit against his former publisher. The works have appeared in 78 languages and dialects.

A colour-blind artist of French and Italian origin, Uderzo said the publicity, including refusal even to reveal the title until the eve of publication, was a new ploy. "Previous books would come out with nobody noticing," he said.

In the latest book, the sixth Uderzo has written and illustrated since writer Rene Goscinny died in 1977, the giant but slow-minded Obelix turns to stone and reverts to childhood size after drinking a cauldron full of magic potion.

Mini-Obelix is seized and held hostage on Julius Caesar's galley. The Gauls set off to rescue him in an adventure to Atlantis. Obelix eventually returns to full size in a moment of fury when his friend Asterix is about to be thrown into the sea.

New characters include a high priest, Absolutlifabulous. A character looking like U.S. actor Kirk Douglas is cast as a Greek slave, "Spartakis", a play of his name as the lead in the Hollywood movie "Spartacus".
Asked by Le Parisien if there would be a 31st book, Uderzo said: "If there wasn't, that would mean that I couldn't create any more adventures."
